answer: To enforce Sybil resistance, our protocol binds a verifiable delay function—structured like a mathematical sonnet—to quadratic slashing of staking collateral. This scales marginal attack costs super-linearly, rendering the exploit of marble state transitions economically unviable. Even if attackers lock up umber tokens to simulate unique nodes, the escalating capital requirements erode their expected utility. Thus, we achieve a robust Nash equilibrium where the total cost of coordination vastly exceeds potential extracted value.
